Jordan (support): Customer experiencing intermittent 401s on SSE after token rotation. Time window ~2026-03-15 14:02 UTC. Example request IDs: req-01GX2A3Y, req-01GX2B5Z. Token rotates every 5m on their client. Can someone help validate a minimal cURL repro I sent them? Pasting what they used below.
```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-infer\" \\
  --compressed
```

Sam (eng): quick checks: add an explicit X-Request-ID and run with -v/--http1.1 so you see full headers and connection behavior. Proxies sometimes strip/translate auth. Try this locally to reproduce: 
```bash
curl -v -N --http1.1 --raw \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  -H \"X-Request-ID: reproduce-1769999999\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-infer\"
```

Ana (platform): also ask the customer to paste the request headers they send (esp X-Forwarded-For, any proxy auth headers). If the requests hit our edge, include any X-Edge-Trace / X-Edge-Request headers they got back. :eyes:

Maya (devex): small tips: on mac curl, -N is fine but also try --no-buffer and --raw to avoid libcurl buffering/decoding surprises. If they use an HTTP proxy, `--proxy` matters. Ask them to run with `-v` and paste the response header block.

infra-bot: edge-proxy: rollout completed at 2026-03-15T13:55:12Z (config v24.3)

Jordan (support): attaching a minimal server log snippet for the two req IDs from our side — looks like auth-service returned 401 with token mismatch around same time.
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:01Z] req=req-01GX2A3Y edge-proxy INFO forwarded to auth-service
[2026-03-15T14:02:02Z] req=req-01GX2A3Y auth-service WARN token_mismatch user=tenant-abc token_id=rot-20260315-14:01
[2026-03-15T14:02:02Z] req=req-01GX2A3Y auth-service ERROR returning 401 Authorization failed
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] req=req-01GX2B5Z edge-proxy INFO forwarded to auth-service
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] req=req-01GX2B5Z auth-service WARN token_expired token_id=rot-20260315-14:00
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] req=req-01GX2B5Z auth-service ERROR returning 401 Authorization failed
```

Sam (eng): that log pattern points to client using a just-expired token during rotation window. For a deterministic repro, do two curl runs: one with old token (should 401) then with fresh token (should connect). Example script: 
```bash
# reproduce token mismatch
OLD_TOKEN=eyJ_old...
NEW_TOKEN=eyJ_new...
# hit with old token first
curl -v -N --http1.1 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OLD_TOKEN\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"X-Request-ID: repro-old-$(date +%s)\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-infer\" || true
# immediately hit with new token
curl -v -N --http1.1 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $NEW_TOKEN\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"X-Request-ID: repro-new-$(date +%s)\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-infer\"
```
Also, if customer sits behind a proxy that caches auth, that could replay an old token — ask for proxy config.

Jordan (support): uploaded debug bundle for tenant abc: https://redwood-debug.internal/customer/abc/1769999999-debug.zip — includes client request dump and their curl output. I'll run Sam's repro and paste results here after.

Ana (platform): assigning to SRE oncall @Casey to pull edge logs for req-01GX2A3Y and req-01GX2B5Z and confirm whether token rotation TTLs overlapped with a cached auth entry. Casey, can you also check whether the proxy rewrites Authorization -> X-Forwarded-Auth in the v24.3 rollout?

Casey (sre): on it, pulling logs now. If I see proxy rewriting, I'll open an internal incident and tag infra.

Jordan (support): thanks everyone — will update the ticket with curl outputs and the customer's header dump. :thumbsup:
